channels.label: IRS Free File (guided tax software)
channels.note: Eight private-sector partners provide guided software free through the IRS. Each partner sets its own extra criteria, which may include age, income, state residency, and military status, so check a few. A partner may charge for a state return.

channels.label: Free File Fillable Forms
channels.note: Open to every income level. These are the electronic forms themselves with no guidance, so they suit someone comfortable preparing their own return. There is always a free federal option, whatever you earn.

channels.label: VITA, free in-person preparation
channels.note: IRS-certified volunteers prepare your return for you, free. Open to people who generally make $69,000 or less, and also to people with disabilities and to taxpayers with limited English proficiency regardless of that figure.

channels.label: TCE, free preparation for people 60 and older
channels.note: No income limit at all. Volunteers specialize in pensions and retirement questions. Most sites are run by the AARP Foundation's Tax-Aide program.

channels.label: MilTax, for the military community
channels.note: Run by the Department of Defense. Free electronic filing of a federal return plus up to three state returns, with no income limit.

omitted.label: IRS Direct File
omitted.reason: The IRS confirmed Direct File is not available for the 2026 filing season, and has set no future launch date. It is listed here so its absence reads as a checked fact rather than an oversight.

citation.sourceDocument: IRS, 2026 tax filing season opens with several free filing options available
citation.sourceNote: Free File guided-software AGI limit of $89,000 for tax year 2025 and the Free File Fillable Forms no-income-limit option are taken from the IRS 2026 filing-season release. The VITA figure (generally $69,000 or less, plus people with disabilities and taxpayers with limited English proficiency) and the TCE age-60-and-older criterion with no income limit come from the IRS Free tax return preparation for qualifying taxpayers page. Direct File is recorded under omitted: the IRS notified states it will not be available in filing season 2026 and set no launch date, and it appears in neither IRS page above. Every figure here is a filing-season threshold that moves annually, so this shard carries no grace year.
